directions: This file configures the LLMs knowledge-builder may use. Nothing is
configured yet: language_models below is the empty base configuration,
and the CLIs keep reporting 'not configured' until it is filled in.
This _help section is documentation only: the program ignores it on load
and drops it when it rewrites the file. Keep extra notes at this top
level too -- inside openai_compatible every key is a provider name, so
comments cannot live there.
OPENAI-COMPATIBLE PROVIDER (OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral,
llama.cpp server, LM Studio, vLLM, ...):
1. Copy openai_compatible_example below into the openai_compatible
section of language_models, renaming its key to your provider name
(that name is what the --provider flag takes).
2. api_url is the endpoint root that serves /chat/completions, usually
ending in /v1 (for example https://api.openai.com/v1).
3. The API key never goes in this file: api_key_title names an entry
in the OS secret store. Store the key under that title with:
python -m knowledge_builder.storage_cli set <api_key_title>
Omit api_key_title for keyless local servers.
4. available_models lists the endpoint's models: name is the model id
the endpoint expects; display_name, max_tokens, reasoning_effort and
capabilities are optional.
OLLAMA (local server, no API key):
1. Copy ollama_example below into language_models as the 'ollama' block,
or edit the one already there.
2. api_url is the server address (http://127.0.0.1:11434); do not add
/v1, the program appends it automatically.
3. Model names are exactly what 'ollama list' shows, tag included (for
example llama3.2:3b). context_window, auto_discover and the
supports_* model flags are optional and informational.
The CLIs pick the first provider and its first model by default;
override with --provider and --model.
